resources.string: Medial view of a normal brain, with the front at left. The pineal body projects behind the upper part of the third ventricle, above the midbrain.
This small epithalamic gland is attached to the back of the third ventricle by a short stalk. It lies above the superior colliculi and is separate from the hypothalamus.
This narrow midline cavity contains cerebrospinal fluid. The pineal body attaches near the junction of its roof and back wall, outside the main cavity.
A small extension of the third ventricle reaches between the upper and lower parts of the pineal stalk. It is a fluid space, not pineal tissue.
This folded, vascular tissue hangs from the roof of the third ventricle and helps make cerebrospinal fluid. It lies above and forward of the pineal body.
One of two rounded elevations at the back of the midbrain, just below the pineal region. The colliculi help orient the eyes and head toward stimuli.
